sentence: Multiply the bottoms together, multiply each top by the other bottom, then add the tops.
You have to find a common bottom. Times the two bottoms, and change each top by multiplying it with the other bottom, then add those tops.
Make the bottoms the same by multiplying, then add the tops.
When the bottoms are the same, keep the bottom and add the tops.
Add the tops and keep the bigger bottom.
Keep doubling both bottoms until they're the same.
Look at the tenths first. The bigger tenth wins. If the tenths are the same, check the next place, and if every place is the same, they're equal.
Compare them place by place starting with the tenths. The first place where they're different decides. If all places match they're equal.
The longer number is bigger because it has more digits.
Add a zero to the shorter one.
